final_steps: Under Dreykov's chemical control, Yelena leads Ingrid and other Widows in Morocco to take an antidote gas from Oksana, an older Widow. Yelena fatally stabs Oksana, who frees her with the gas and tells her to free the others.
Ingrid reports to Dreykov that Yelena has deserted and asks to activate the Taskmaster Protocol, and Lerato fits a chip into Taskmaster's helmet.
In Budapest, Ingrid and other Widows attack Natasha and Yelena. Badly hurt in a fall, Ingrid says she is being made to do it, then kills herself.
In the Red Room, Dreykov orders the Widows, Lerato among them, to kill Natasha, and they overpower her until Yelena frees them with the antidote gas.
A freed Widow asks in Finnish what they do now, and Natasha tells them to get as far away as they can and make their own choices.
Natasha tells Yelena to be the one to free the Widows still under control, and Yelena leaves with the freed Widows, Lerato among them, and Antonia.

Yelena and Sonya, who are freeing Widows with the antidote, break into the home of another former Widow, Ana, and spray her with it. It does nothing, because Ana was not brainwashed, and she says she pays for the house by killing for money.
Yelena vanishes from Ana's bathroom and returns five years later to find Ana married with an adopted daughter. Ana offers her a place to stay, and Yelena asks her for help finding Natasha.
In Macau, Helen, freed from the Red Room, fights an Extremis-powered man at Xialing's fight club, then tends to his wounds.
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
Yelena relives her first Red Room test, in which as a girl she leads a fellow trainee, Anya, to be shot.

agent_carter_ruling: Separate file. The Agent Carter#5 school does not belong in 'The Widows' file with Dreykov's Red Room Widows. Reasons: (1) On screen the girls are never called Widows, and Wikipedia's summary calls the place a 'Soviet military complex' where girls train as sleeper agents. Linking it to the Black Widow program comes from off-screen statements by the producers ('the precursor to the Black Widow Program', IGN 2015, cited on Wikipedia). (2) It is Leviathan's program of 1937 to 1946, with no Dreykov, no chemical control and no antidote, so it cannot share this file's story. The file's group statuses (At large, then Allied after Yelena's gas) would mean nothing across a nine-year gap and a different group. (3) Every Widow named in the file's steps belongs to Dreykov's generation. Recommendation: give the school's girls their own collective file, or attach them to Leviathan's file. Dottie already has her own file (st-dottie-underwood). That file would need Anya and Eva, with verified wording such as: Agent Carter#5, 'In a Soviet school that trains girls as assassins, young Dottie and her friend Anya share hidden bread, then Dottie breaks Anya's neck in sparring when the headmistress nods.' (At large); Agent Carter#5, 'When Peggy's team storms the school, a girl named Eva fakes tears, stabs Dugan in his vest and kills Junior Juniper with his gun before escaping into a vent. In the firefight that follows she shoots Agent Li dead and wounds Happy Sam.' (At large). Sources: https://marvelcinematicuniverse.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&prop=wikitext&format=json&page=The_Iron_Ceiling ; https://marvelcinematicuniverse.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&prop=wikitext&format=json&page=Eva ; https://marvelcinematicuniverse.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&prop=wikitext&format=json&page=Anya_(USSR_Red_Room) ; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?action=raw&title=Agent_Carter_season_1 .

other_findings: Coverage check under the owner's rule. These Sacred Timeline Widows have no file of their own, and all are now named with their on-screen actions: Oksana, Ingrid, Lerato, the Finnish-speaking Widow (unnamed, so she is described rather than named), Sonya, Ana, Helen and Anya (Thunderbolts*). These have their own files and need no step: Natasha, Yelena, Melina, Antonia/Taskmaster, Ruth Bat-Seraph and Dottie.

Helen in Black Widow: on screen she chokes Natasha with a staff before the gas frees her (MCU wiki), but no name is said or credited in that film. She is named only from Shang-Chi on, so the Shang-Chi step is where she is named.
Ingrid: the Budapest Widow who kills herself and the Ingrid on the radio in Morocco are the same credited character (Wikipedia cast list; MCU wiki).
Antonia: controlled by the Red Room but never shown training as a Widow. She has her own file (taskmaster), and her death in Thunderbolts* belongs there.
Hawkeye#5 opens with a voice-over replay of Natasha's line from Black Widow ('He had widows implanted all over the world... you should be the one to tell 'em it's over') before Ana's scene.
Ana also tells Yelena that Sonya left her house 'in a much less dramatic fashion', which confirms on screen that Sonya survives the Blip.

Statuses: steps 1 to 3 are 'At large' (the Widows are under Dreykov's control and hunting). From the gas onward the steps are 'Allied'. The Thunderbolts* step is a flashback, but it keeps 'Allied' because the status describes the group at that point in the story.
The Morocco setting comes from the plot summaries on both wikis. The transcript does not include on-screen location cards.
The MCU wiki has a contradiction in Agent Carter#5. The Anya (USSR Red Room) page says Dottie hides the bread and shares it, while The Iron Ceiling episode page says Anya does. Use neutral wording.

Transcript source: springfieldspringfield.co.uk for Black Widow, Hawkeye 1x05, Shang-Chi and Thunderbolts*. No transcript was found for Agent Carter 1x05, so those points rest on the MCU wiki and Wikipedia.
